answer:
Yes, but the mail shows the pushback only from October 2001. Before that, the group did valuation work on LJM deals without any objection I could find.

**Earlier work, no objection found**
- On 1999-12-27, Stinson Gibner sent a spreadsheet valuing the "RTHM put position" under the subject "LJM put valuation".
- On 2000-02-16, Paulo Issler reported presenting a two-factor model for calculating credit loss on the LJM position to Accounting and Credit. Credit seemed positive about the approach.
- On 2001-09-06, Issler added a valuation of the combined Peregrine and Shortfall restrictions to a spreadsheet for Ron. This was for "Raptor Discount Valuations".
- My searches turned up no mail in which the group objected to LJM before October 2001. That is a gap in what I found, not proof that no objection existed.

**The October 2001 pushback**
- **2001-10-04:** Kaminski wrote to Ryan Siurek, copying Rick Buy and David Port. He said he "cannot support the valuations my group has produced so far for the LJM/Raptor related transactions without examination of all the related legal documents." He added that the transactions "are too complex and controversial to bypass due diligence requirements." He also said the group "did solid work based on verbal information", so this was a challenge to the lack of documents, not to the quality of the group's own work.
- **2001-10-22:** Rakesh Bharati forwarded a request from Arthur Andersen's Kimberly Scardino for the latest Raptor valuation memo. Kaminski replied to Bharati and Vasant Shanbhogue. He said the legal documents "were not provided and therefore we cannot sign off on any analysis done in the past."
- In the same reply, he told them to inform Andersen "I cannot support the quantitative analysis we have done in the past," and said he was "especially concerned about the conflict between the existence of the restriction and the existence of a put that are, in my view, mutually exclusive." This is the strongest statement, and he sent it to two of his own people.
- The wider group was involved in the valuation work. Issler's September mail refers to an approach he and "Vassant" had discussed.

**What happened afterwards**
- On 2001-11-01, Rick Buy forwarded Kaminski's Oct 4 message with "FYI". The mail I found doesn't show what Buy did with it or how Siurek responded.
- On 2001-12-19, Kaminski sent the Oct 4 text to an outside lawyer (dcohen@wilmer.com), saying it was "stored on my PC at home" and "disappeared from my mailbox on the Enron system." The email doesn't say why it disappeared. Other copies are still in the store, including Buy's forward and Kaminski's own forwards of 2001-11-06.

**Limits.** The pushback was Kaminski's own written position, and it was narrow: no sign-off without the contracts. I found no email in which he objected to LJM's existence or its conflicts of interest. The mail doesn't show whether anyone acted on it.
